DILG • BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City D'LG No. OCT 29 HON. MYCA ELIZABETH R. VERGARA City Mayor Cabanatuan City Province of Nueva Ecija Dear Mayor Vergara: This has reference to your letter dated 20 August 2024 requesting for this Department's opinion concerning the power of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to review ordinances of its component city. In your letter, you informed the Department of the following salient facts and circumstances: I. 2. The City of Cabanatuan passed and submitted City Ordinance No. 026- 2024, Series of 2024, entitled, "An Ordinance Approving the Schedule of Goodwill Rates for Specific Stalls/Spaces in the New City Supermarket and New Magsaysay Public Market and Adopting the Guidelines on the Awards of Market Stall Thereof' The Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Nueva Ecija, in its Resolution No. 284-S- 2024 dated 30 April 2024 disapproved the aforesaid City Ordinance, due to the following grounds: a. b. c. d. The goodwill fees imposed contravenes Section 186 of the LGC for being unjust, excessive, and oppressive. The goodwill fees imposed do not promote the general welfare of the constituents of the City of Cabanatuan (Section 16 of the LGC). The goodwill fees imposed will not upgrade the quality of life of the people but will rather burden and hinder their economic development (Section 5(c) of the LGC). Certain provision of the ordinance are vague and confusing such as: i. Section 3 of the of the ordinance specifies a 30-year long-term lease and therefore it can be construed that goodwill can be paid in 30 years. However, Section 4(lV) — Procedure for Awarding of Stalls, provides that 50% of the total goodwill shall be paid within 3 days from notice and the remaining 50% shall be paid upon notice "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline NO. (02) 8876 3454

ii. before occupancy. Section 4, paragraph K is not favorable to the stakeholders. Best efforts should be exerted to ensure that the constructed stalls are accurate in size, as planned. Bidders should not be burdened by inconsistencies and errors in the markets' construction. 3. The ordinance failed to clearly set the monthly fees due to each stallholder, and the monthly fees will be based on the projection of the Local Finance Committee and this can be deemed as undue delegation of legislative power. Based on the foregoing submission, posed for this Department's opinion is whether or not the invalidation of City Ordinance No. 026-2024, Series of 2024, by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Nueva Ecija is in excess of and beyond its review powers. At the outset, Memorandum Order No. 2010-02 dated 17 September 2010 provides that the Department shall not act on queries of the following kinds, to wit: 1. 2. 3. Those containinq facts that are justiciable in nature. Justiciable issues are those that require adjudication by the courts of law as to who between the opposing parties have the better right over a qiven controversy: Those presumptively valid acts, e.g., enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances; Those that are litis pendencia or pending litigation, except when the court itself requests for the opinion. In the event that an opinion has been rendered by the Department and its field officers without knowledge or information that a case involving the issues raised in the query is pending in court, such opinion shall automatically be deemed ineffective; and Those that are cognizable by other agencies of the government. In this regard, considering that the matter at hand is justiciable in nature as it may ripen into a full-blown litigation, We are proscribed from issuing our opinion. Nonetheless, for purposes of academic discussion only, allow us to generally answer your queries. In reply to your query, may we invite your attention to Section 56 of Republic Act No. 7160, also known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), viz: Section 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (c) If the sangguniang panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in pan. The sangguniang panlalawigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. It is clear from the foregoing that the sole ground to declare an ordinance or Page 2 of 2

resolution invalid, in whole or in part, is when the same is beyond the power conferred upon the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned. In relation thereto, in the landmark case of Moday vs. CA', the Supreme Court, citing Velasco vs. Blas, ruled that: "The only qround upon which a provincial board may declare any municipal resolution, ordinance, or order invalid is when such resolution, ordinance or order is "beyond the power conferred upon the council or president making the same". Absolutely, no other ground is recognized by the law. A strictly Ieqal question is before the provincial board in is consideration of a municipal resolution, ordinance or order The provincial board's disapproval of any resolution, ordinance or order must be premised specifically upon the fact that such resolution, ordinance or order is outside the scope of legal powers conferred by law. If a provincial board passes these limits, it usurps the legislative functions of the municipal council, or president. " (emphasis and underscoring supplied) To reiterate the Court's pronouncement in Moday, the review of a city or municipal ordinance, resolution or order must be confined to a strict legal question on whether such ordinance, resolution, or order is "beyond the power conferred upon the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned". This excludes a determination on the wisdom and propriety of a legislative enactment. This opinion is rendered based solely on the facts presented and our appreciation of the same without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of other government agencies and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours: ORITY OF THE SE TARY: ATTY. J R. LLAMAS retary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELL JVRULLLS-LRALLD/jvpr G.R.
